title: Weekly pilot quality sync + regression & guardrail triage with Treeline Financial
summary: Weekly POC sync to review scoring regressions on the expense-categorization pilot, triage guardrail failures, and decide next steps toward a focused benchmark on dedicated capacity. Key asks: run 1k synthetic samples on dedicated instance, share SOC2 / KMS docs, and adjust scoring thresholds and rule-based overrides.
topics: dedicated vs hosted capacity for benchmarks
next_steps: Redwood to run 1k-sample regression on dedicated pool and share token-level latency/cost breakdown by 2025-08-05
Treeline to provide 500 labeled edge-case prompts and updated acceptance thresholds by 2025-08-04
Redwood to circulate SOC2 audit summary and KMS integration guide by 2025-07-31
Schedule engineering deep-dive for model routing and canary rollback on 2025-08-07
action_items: Raj Patel (Redwood SE): Execute 1,000-sample run on Redwood Dedicated replica, capture latency and per-route tokens, due 2025-08-05
Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Share security pack (SOC2 summary, KMS/SSO notes) and pricing sketch for a short dedicated pilot, due 2025-07-31
Priya Shah (Treeline PM): Upload 500 labeled failure cases and mark severity (blocker/major/minor), due 2025-08-04
Connor Li (Treeline Sec): Confirm any required IP allowlists and provide KMS key policy questions, due 2025-08-01
Elena Ortiz (Redwood CSM): Schedule 60-min deep-dive and include capacity sizing estimate, by 2025-08-07
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-07-30 14:05 PDT
- Duration: 57 mins
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Raj (Redwood SE), Elena (CSM), Adrian (Treeline Head ML), Priya (PM), Connor (Security), Dana (Data)

Summary / Purpose: quick weekly checkpoint for the expense categorization POC. Review the latest scorecard, triage recent guardrail hits, and decide whether to spin up a dedicated benchmark to reproduce regressions.

00:00:05 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll go for about an hour today, main goals are to look at the scoring regression that popped up last week and triage the guardrail false positives
00:00:12 Adrian Gomez: yep thanks Maya, quick note we saw a drop in micro-F1 on merchant extraction around tuesday, a lot more miscategorizations for international vendors
00:00:30 Raj Patel: ok can you point to a specific example? like is this latency induced truncation or prompt drift?
00:00:38 Dana Brooks: here's an example, invoice_1234, vendor shows as "N-Vendor Co" and model returned 'Miscellaneous' instead of 'Travel' — seems like some tokenization oddities with non-ascii characters
00:00:55 Priya Shah: also noticed the score threshold we set at 0.65 is letting through ambiguous labels, maybe we need a two-tier scoring + rule override
00:01:10 Elena Ortiz: quick clarifier — are we confident this started after the prompt changes on 7/22 or earlier?
00:01:20 Adrian Gomez: timeline looks aligned with the prompt compacting we did on 7/22 to reduce tokens, could be that the shorter context lost vendor cues
00:01:45 Raj Patel: right, we've seen compaction reduce context signal. Two immediate handles: restore some of the optional context or introduce a small reranker step on top for vendor extraction
00:02:05 Connor Li: on the security side, if we move to a dedicated pool to reproduce this, we need to confirm KMS integration and IP allowlisting. I posted a note in the tracker.
00:02:22 Maya Chen: we can share the KMS and SOC2 docs today, we'll also note differences between hosted and Redwood Dedicate (auto-transcribed in the notes) — sorry that was, Redwood Dedicated
00:02:40 Priya Shah: can you outline the cost delta? Treeline is sensitive to monthly spend while POC-ing stuff
00:02:52 Maya Chen: absolutely; rough numbers: hosted run small, per-token; dedicated has base reserved + lower per-token on heavy throughput. We'll send a short sketch after the call.
00:03:10 Adrian Gomez: what about latency? for our UI we need 200-500ms tail for single-shot vendor extraction calls, batching isn't an option for interactive flows
00:03:25 Raj Patel: our runtime can be tuned for low tail latency with lower batch sizes and KV cache warmups, but yes that will increase unit cost. We can show a latency vs cost curve from a dedicated run
00:03:45 Dana Brooks: the scorecard shows two predominant failure modes: hallucinated vendor names and label mixing where travel and meals get swapped
00:04:02 Priya Shah: there are also guardrail false positives — the profanity/PII detector is flagging bank names like 'First National' as PII sometimes
00:04:18 Raj Patel: interesting, that's likely a lexicon overlap. We can tune the guardrail rules to whitelist known vendor tokens and also adjust the detector sensitivity for the finance vertical
00:04:35 Adrian Gomez: is there an easy way to add a rule-based layer that short-circuits the ML output when confidence low?
00:04:45 Raj Patel: yes — you can do a hybrid flow: ML proposes candidate + confidence, then rules apply. For low confidence, call a secondary, more conservative prompt or fallback label
00:05:00 Priya Shah: do we have examples where fallback would've fixed it?
00:05:07 Dana Brooks: we tried a deterministic regex on vendor tax ids and it corrected ~12% of the incidents but missed name variants
00:05:25 Maya Chen: ok so two parallel tracks: 1) reproduce and quantify on dedicated to get token/latency/cost numbers; 2) tune prompt and scoring thresholds plus ruleset + reranker to lower false positives
00:05:40 Connor Li: a note on data privacy — if we upload Redacted PII to dedicated cluster, we need KMS + audit logs turned on, and proof that logs aren't shipped to external analytics by default
00:05:58 Raj Patel: yes logging controls are available, we can toggle retention and redact prefixes. We'll include the logging config snippet in the security pack
00:06:12 Adrian Gomez: about scoring regressions — can you break down if the drop is model-change related vs prompt distribution shift?
00:06:22 Raj Patel: initial look: model version hasn't changed on our side; more likely distribution shift due to longer vendor strings and international characters. But we should test older prompt set vs new compact prompts side-by-side on the same model and infra
00:06:45 Priya Shah: would it help to reintroduce some of the original context window for merchant lines? we can drop other non-critical fields
00:06:55 Raj Patel: yes, adding 64 tokens of merchant context back often recovers signal without big token cost increase
00:07:10 Maya Chen: action: Raj will run side-by-side: compact prompt vs expanded prompt on dedicated replica for 1k records, capture micro-F1, latency, and cost-per-1k tokens
00:07:25 Dana Brooks: if you can also capture the guardrail false positive count per config that'd be great
00:07:32 Raj Patel: will do, I'll include guardrail hits in the output csv
00:07:40 Adrian Gomez: about reranker — what's the recommended approach? small local model reranker or second-pass prompt-based verification?
00:07:52 Raj Patel: for speed we often use a lightweight reranker (a distilled smaller LM) for candidates; if that's not available, a focused prompt verification pass works but increases latency
00:08:10 Priya Shah: tradeoff again — cost vs latency. We'll prioritize correctness for now but want options for the interactive path later
00:08:25 Maya Chen: question for Connor — what level of SOC2 artifact is sufficient for Treeline legal?
00:08:33 Connor Li: summary report + gap list is usually ok for initial evaluation. Our legal team will ask for the full attestation if we progress to procurement
00:08:45 Maya Chen: we can share the SOC2 summary and KMS integration guide by tomorrow, and a pointer to the full report under NDA if needed
00:08:54 Priya Shah: thanks — also can you share the scorecard spreadsheet with per-prompt buckets and the heatmap?
00:09:04 Elena Ortiz: we'll post the updated scorecard, but note some of the heatmap labels were slightly off due to utf-8 parsing — apologies for the noise
00:09:18 Adrian Gomez: ok, small tangent — we saw higher tokenization cost for some euro currencies, is that expected?
00:09:30 Raj Patel: yes special characters and currency symbols can expand token counts depending on tokenizer; we can preprocess or normalize currencies to reduce variability
00:09:45 Dana Brooks: on the labeled edge cases, our team will add severity tags and whether a rule-based override would be acceptable
00:09:58 Priya Shah: timeline: we want to decide on dedicated benchmark within two weeks if regressions persist
00:10:10 Maya Chen: that aligns with our proposal — dedicated short pilot of 2 weeks with reserved nodes to reproduce at scale
00:10:22 Adrian Gomez: also one more thing: any known regressions introduced by quantization profiles? we briefly tested int8 last month
00:10:34 Raj Patel: quantization can increase hallucination risk depending on model; we'll note which profile we use for the dedicated run and can compare float16 vs int8 quickly
00:10:50 Connor Li: from security: quantization isn't a blocker but we need to ensure model weights aren't exported in an insecure way — we'll check that in the security pack
00:11:02 Maya Chen: sounds good. Now let's walk through the example logs we uploaded in the drive
00:11:10 Priya Shah: (screen share) here's the scorecard: folder -> scorecards -> treeline_july_v2.xlsx
00:11:25 Dana Brooks: note the 'confusion matrix' sheet — the travel vs meals swap is concentrated in vendor substrings with '&' and accents
00:11:40 Raj Patel: thanks, that matches the tokenizer observation. I'll include a normalized pipeline as a quick preprocessing step to strip diacritics for vendor matching
00:11:55 Adrian Gomez: can Redwood also try a secondary confirmatory prompt that asks for explicit vendor canonicalization? only invoked when confidence < 0.5
00:12:08 Raj Patel: yes that's doable — it's a low-impact conditional call. We'll model cost in the dedication run
00:12:20 Maya Chen: moving to guardrail hits — we logged 23 guardrail flags last week, about 8 were false positives per your labeling
00:12:32 Dana Brooks: examples include 'First National Bank' flagged as PII and company registration numbers mis-tagged as SSN
00:12:44 Raj Patel: whitelist-based approach + relaxed regex thresholds for finance vertical should reduce FP; we'll test before and after counts
00:12:58 Priya Shah: can we get an automated daily digest of guardrail hits so we can triage quickly?
:00:13:07 Elena Ortiz: yes, Redwood Console supports scheduled alerts and an export; I'll configure a daily digest for Treeline and share the subscription link
00:13:20 Adrian Gomez: excellent. Ok any other blockers?
00:13:25 Connor Li: just the allowlist/KMS questions, but we'll follow up via the tracker after we see the security pack
00:13:35 Maya Chen: perfect. quick recap: Raj runs 1k side-by-side (compact vs expanded prompts) on a dedicated replica, include latency, token counts, guardrail hits and compare quantization profiles. Redwood shares SOC2/KMS docs + pricing sketch. Treeline supplies 500 labeled edge cases. Schedule deep dive week after next.
00:13:58 Priya Shah: sounds good. thanks everyone.
00:14:05 Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up in the thread with artifacts. bye.

Post-call notes: the transcript engine mis-labeled 'Redwood Dedicated' once; some utf-8 vendor names were scrambled in the scorecard export. Links shared during call: https://drive.company/scorecards/treeline_july_v2.xlsx (scorecard), https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (placeholder).
notes: Transcript contains typical ASR errors (vendor diacritics, 'Redwood Dedicate' mis-transcription). Customer prioritized accuracy over marginal latency improvements; security wants KMS + allowlist proof before dedicated access. Action owners assigned.
